title: 2 xTradescantia Zebrina Flame Dance - Mini Houseplant - Easy Care Hardy
description:
Tradescantia zebrina ‘Flame Dance’
 
 is a distinctive trailing tropical plant valued for its unusual, variable foliage. The stems are smooth and speckled green, while the leaves feature silver bands that may appear as broken streaks or be completely absent. Depending on growing conditions, leaf colour can range from olive green and silver to deep red and purple tones. Leaf undersides are a rich purplish red, adding strong contrast when displayed in hanging baskets or on shelves. Although it occasionally produces small lavender or white flowers (about 1 cm in diameter) from July to October, it is primarily grown for its striking foliage.


  Growing Conditions:
 

   Temperature:
  
  Tender perennial – keep frost-free (best suited for indoor cultivation in the UK or greenhouse conditions).
 

   Light:
  
  Prefers bright, indirect light or part shade. Intense light enhances purple and red tones, but full sun may cause scorching.
 

   Soil:
  
  Use a free-draining compost mix with good moisture retention, such as a peat-free or coir-based houseplant compost.
 

   Watering:
  
  Keep the soil evenly moist during the growing season; reduce watering in autumn and winter. Avoid waterlogging.
 

   Feeding:
  
  Apply a balanced liquid houseplant fertiliser monthly in spring and summer.
 

   Maintenance:
  
  Easy to grow and low maintenance. Trim or pinch out growing tips to encourage bushy growth. Propagate easily by stem cuttings.
 

  Plant Details:
 

   Mature size:
  
  Height approx. 30 cm, spread up to 25 cm
 

   Type:
  
  Tender perennial, semi-trailing or prostrate habit
 

   Flowering:
  
  July–October (lavender or white flowers about 1 cm across)
 

   Position:
  
  Part shade, bright filtered light indoors
 

  Background:
 

 The cultivar
 
  ‘Flame Dance’
 
 belongs to
 
  Tradescantia zebrina
 
 , a tropical species often grown as a decorative houseplant for its metallic foliage. The name ‘Flame Dance’ was first circulated online in 2020 and formally described in print in 2022. It is occasionally mislabelled as
 
  ‘Purple Rain’
 
 or
 
  ‘Green Ghost’
 
 . Like other forms of
 
  Tradescantia zebrina
 
 , this plant’s appearance can change with light intensity and environmental conditions, making each specimen slightly unique.


  Issues:
 

 Overly wet soil may lead to root rot. Watch for common houseplant pests such as mealybugs, aphids, and spider mites.
